_about: A/B take-profit variants derived from the Revelio Trading TJR backtest findings (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4uqeKO6KcJk). Each variant is an `overrides` dict keyed on the 7 TP A/B fields used by BacktestsPage.tsx (TP_AB_FIELDS). Only these keys differ between variants; every other strategy param is inherited from your base form (i.e. your live config). Paste the `overrides` of each into a variant slot, or load this file. partial_profit_r: 0 = disabled (single target). ifvg_tp1_fraction = fraction taken at TP1. ifvg_be_after_tp1 = move stop to breakeven after TP1. htf_target_enabled = use structural HTF target instead of fixed r_multiple. Compare variants on TOTAL REALIZED R, not hit rate.

variants.name: Baseline 3-tier partials + BE (the structure under critique)
variants.rationale: Replicates the TJR-style partial-scaling-with-breakeven the video shows quietly damages payoff. This is your control.

variants.name: Single fixed target, no partials, no BE (full-size winners)
variants.rationale: Directly tests the video's core claim: letting the full position run to one target beats fractioning winners while losers stay full -1R. Pure single-R exit.

variants.name: Single fixed target 3R, no partials (higher fixed R)
variants.rationale: Tests whether a wider single target (no scaling) captures the runners the partial structure gives away. Same family as B but more aggressive R.

variants.name: Runner-weighted partials (small TP1, let most ride)
variants.rationale: If partials help psychologically, take only a SMALL fraction at TP1 and let the majority run, instead of equal thirds. Tests whether reducing the cut-fraction fixes the payoff asymmetry.

variants.name: Partials WITHOUT breakeven move
variants.rationale: Isolates the cost of the breakeven-after-TP1 rule. Same partials as A but the stop does NOT trail to BE, so winners aren't choked off by noise stop-outs.

variants.name: Structural HTF target, no fixed-R cap, no partials
variants.rationale: Tests target placement at real structure (HTF) vs a fixed R-multiple, with full-size position. The video argues fixed multi-tier targets are arbitrary; structural targets may capture the true move.
